description: Debug & Diagnostics page (Settings > Advanced) -- provides developer tools for troubleshooting GUI automation. The page contains two main sections: Debug Settings for configuring image match debug mode and top match candidate count, and Device Information for viewing and copying system identifiers (Device ID, Device Name, Platform). The page loads settings from the Rust backend via Tauri IPC commands and persists changes on explicit save. Device info supports copy-to-clipboard with visual feedback.

groups.name: Initial Loading State
groups.description: When the page first mounts, it loads debug settings and device info from the Tauri backend. During this time, a loading indicator is shown. Both loadSettings() and loadDeviceInfo() are called on mount.

assertions.description: While debug settings are loading, users see a 'Loading settings...' status message centered in the page area, indicating the backend is being queried
assertions.expected: Loading message is shown briefly on mount before settings load completes

assertions.description: The loading status element has data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='loading settings' for programmatic detection by automation tools

groups.name: Section Header
groups.description: The page header displays an 'Advanced' title with a wrench icon and a description explaining the purpose of the debug settings. This uses the shared SectionHeader component.

assertions.description: Users see the section title 'Advanced' at the top of the page, establishing context that these are developer/debugging options
Below the title, users see a description explaining these are 'Developer and debugging options for troubleshooting automation issues'
assertions.expected: Developer and debugging options for troubleshooting automation issues

assertions.description: A wrench icon is displayed next to the title, visually indicating this is a tools/configuration section
assertions.expected: A wrench/tool icon appears adjacent to the 'Advanced' heading

groups.name: Error Display
groups.description: When settings fail to load or save, an error banner is displayed with a red X icon and the error message. The error state is set when Tauri IPC calls fail.

assertions.description: When a settings load or save operation fails, an error banner appears with the error message so users understand what went wrong
assertions.expected: Error banner is only visible when there is an error; it shows the specific failure message
assertions.precondition: A settings load or save operation has failed

assertions.description: When the user initiates a new save operation, the previous error is cleared before the new attempt
assertions.expected: Clicking save clears any existing error banner before attempting the save operation
assertions.precondition: An error banner is currently displayed

groups.name: Save Success Feedback
groups.description: After successfully saving settings, a green success banner appears for 3 seconds showing 'Settings saved successfully!'. The save button also briefly changes to show a checkmark and 'Saved!' text.

assertions.description: After a successful save, a success banner appears with 'Settings saved successfully!' message and a checkmark icon, confirming the operation
assertions.expected: Success banner appears immediately after save and auto-dismisses after approximately 3 seconds
assertions.precondition: User has clicked Save and the operation succeeded

assertions.description: The success banner automatically disappears after 3 seconds without user interaction
assertions.expected: After ~3 seconds, the success banner is removed from the DOM

groups.name: Debug Settings Section
groups.description: The Debug section is contained within a rounded card with a 'Debug' heading. It holds the image match debug toggle, the top matches count slider, and an informational note about when settings take effect.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Debug' sub-heading within the settings card, grouping the image-match diagnostic options
The debug settings are wrapped in a rounded card container with subtle background, visually grouping all debug controls together
assertions.expected: The Debug heading and its controls are inside a visually distinct card/container

groups.name: Image Match Debug Mode Toggle
groups.description: A toggle switch labeled 'Enable Image Match Debug Mode' controls whether detailed match information is collected during image recognition. The toggle has a title and a description explaining what it does. Toggling changes local state; changes are not persisted until the user clicks Save.

assertions.description: Users see 'Enable Image Match Debug Mode' as the toggle label, clearly indicating what the setting controls
Below the toggle label, users see a description explaining that it collects and displays detailed match information including top match candidates, confidence scores, and failure diagnostics

criteria.textContent: Collect and display detailed match information

assertions.expected: confidence scores

assertions.description: Users can click the toggle switch to change the image debug mode state. The toggle visually moves between on and off positions
assertions.expected: Clicking the toggle changes its visual state between on (colored/active) and off (muted/inactive)

assertions.description: Toggling the switch only changes local state; the setting is not sent to the backend until the user clicks Save Debug Settings
assertions.expected: Changing the toggle does not trigger a save; only clicking the Save button persists the change

groups.name: Top Matches Count Control
groups.description: A range slider with a companion number input allows users to set how many top match candidates are displayed in debug information. The value is clamped between 1 and 10. Both the slider and the number input are synchronized.

assertions.description: Users see 'Top Matches to Display' as the label for the slider control
A description explains the slider controls 'Number of top match candidates to show in debug information (1-10)'
The range slider has min=1 and max=10, ensuring users can only select values within the valid range
A number input next to the slider shows the current value and stays synchronized with the slider position. Users can type a value directly
assertions.expected: Changing the slider updates the number input, and vice versa. Both reflect the same clamped value (1-10)

assertions.description: The default value for top matches is 5 when no saved settings exist
assertions.precondition: No previously saved debug settings exist

groups.name: Settings Effect Note
groups.description: An informational note below the debug controls explains when settings take effect. This helps users understand they need to run a new image recognition attempt to see changes.

assertions.description: Users see a note explaining 'Debug settings take effect on the next image recognition attempt', informing them that changes are not retroactive
assertions.expected: next image recognition attempt

assertions.description: The note references the 'Image Recognition Debug tab' where debug output will appear
assertions.expected: Image Recognition Debug tab

assertions.description: The note has a 'Note:' label in bold/foreground color followed by muted description text, and is displayed in a subtle primary-tinted background container

groups.name: Save Debug Settings Button
groups.description: A save button at the bottom right of the debug section persists all debug settings to the backend. It shows different states: default ('Save Debug Settings' with a gear icon), saving ('Saving...' with spinner), and saved ('Saved!' with checkmark). The button is disabled during save operations.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Save Debug Settings' button with a settings icon, positioned at the bottom right of the debug section
While a save operation is in progress, the save button is disabled and shows 'Saving...' with a spinner animation, preventing double-submission
assertions.expected: During save: button is disabled, text changes to 'Saving...', a spinning loader appears. After save: button re-enables
assertions.precondition: User has clicked the save button

assertions.description: After a successful save, the button briefly shows 'Saved!' with a checkmark icon before reverting to the default state
assertions.expected: Button shows 'Saved!' with checkmark for ~3 seconds, then returns to 'Save Debug Settings'
assertions.precondition: Save operation has just completed successfully

assertions.description: Clicking save calls the Tauri IPC command 'set_debug_settings' with the current enable_image_debug and top_matches_count values
assertions.expected: The save action invokes 'set_debug_settings' with enableImageDebug (boolean) and topMatchesCount (number) parameters

groups.name: Device Information Section
groups.description: A separate card section shows system device information useful for debugging and support. It has a 'Device Information' heading with a monitor icon, a refresh button, a description, and three device fields: Device ID, Device Name, and Platform. Each field is clickable to copy its value to the clipboard.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Device Information' heading with a monitor icon, identifying this as the system info section
A description tells users this information is 'useful for debugging and support' and that they can 'Click to copy values'
assertions.expected: Click to copy values

assertions.description: A refresh button (circular arrow icon) in the device info header allows users to reload device information from the backend
assertions.expected: A small refresh/reload icon button appears in the Device Information header row, to the right of the heading

groups.name: Device ID Field
groups.description: The Device ID field displays the unique device identifier in monospace font. It is a clickable row that copies the ID to clipboard when clicked, with visual feedback showing a checkmark when copied.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Device ID' label above the device ID value
The Device ID value is displayed in a monospace font, appropriate for technical identifiers
assertions.expected: The device ID value uses a monospace/code font family

assertions.description: Clicking the Device ID row copies the device ID to the clipboard and shows a checkmark icon as feedback
assertions.expected: Clicking the row copies the ID to clipboard. The copy icon changes to a green checkmark for ~2 seconds, then reverts

groups.name: Device Name Field
groups.description: The Device Name field shows the human-readable name of the device. Like the Device ID, it is clickable for copy-to-clipboard functionality.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Device Name' label above the device name value
Clicking the Device Name row copies the name to clipboard with checkmark feedback
assertions.expected: Clicking copies the device name to clipboard. Copy icon changes to checkmark for ~2 seconds

groups.name: Platform Field
groups.description: The Platform field shows the operating system/platform name with text-capitalize CSS, so values like 'windows' display as 'Windows'. It also supports copy-to-clipboard.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Platform' label above the platform value
The platform value is displayed with CSS capitalize, so 'windows' appears as 'Windows', 'macos' as 'Macos', etc.
assertions.expected: capitalize

assertions.description: Clicking the Platform row copies the platform value to clipboard with checkmark feedback
assertions.expected: Clicking copies the platform name to clipboard. Copy icon changes to checkmark for ~2 seconds

groups.name: Device Info Loading State
groups.description: While device info is being fetched from the backend, a loading indicator with a spinning refresh icon and 'Loading device info...' text is shown in place of the device fields.

assertions.description: While device info is loading, users see 'Loading device info...' with a spinning refresh icon
assertions.expected: The loading message is shown only when deviceInfoLoading is true and deviceInfo is null (initial load)

assertions.description: The loading status element has data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='loading device info' for automation detection

groups.name: Device Info Unavailable State
groups.description: When device info fails to load (deviceInfo is null after loading completes), an italic message 'Unable to load device information.' is shown instead of the device fields.

assertions.description: When device info fails to load, users see an italic 'Unable to load device information.' message
assertions.precondition: Device info API call has failed or returned null

assertions.description: The unavailable message has data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='device info unavailable' for automation tools
assertions.precondition: Device info is null after loading attempt

groups.name: Device ID Tip Note
groups.description: Below the device fields, a tip note encourages users to include their Device ID when reporting issues.

assertions.description: Users see a tip note that says to include Device ID when reporting issues to help identify the runner in the system
assertions.expected: reporting issues

assertions.description: The tip note has a bold 'Tip:' label prefix in foreground color

groups.name: Tauri IPC Integration
groups.description: The Debug page integrates with the Rust backend through three Tauri IPC commands: 'get_debug_settings' (load on mount), 'set_debug_settings' (save button), and 'get_device_info' (load on mount + refresh). These are the data sources for all displayed information.

assertions.description: On component mount, the page calls 'get_debug_settings' to load saved debug settings from the Rust backend
assertions.expected: The Tauri invoke('get_debug_settings') is called once on mount. On success with data, settings (enable_image_debug, top_matches_count) are populated. On failure, default values are used.

assertions.description: On component mount, the page calls 'get_device_info' to load device identification from the Rust backend
assertions.expected: The Tauri invoke('get_device_info') is called once on mount. On success, device_id, device_name, and platform are displayed. On failure, the 'Unable to load' message appears.

assertions.description: Clicking the refresh button in the Device Information header calls 'get_device_info' again, with the spinner animation showing during the reload
assertions.expected: Clicking refresh: sets deviceInfoLoading=true (spinner animates), calls get_device_info, updates displayed data on success, stops spinner on completion

groups.name: Overall Page Layout
groups.description: The Debug page is rendered inside the Settings container which provides a full-height flex layout with padding and scrollable content. The page itself uses a space-y-6 vertical layout with the section header at top, then the debug settings card, then the device information card.

assertions.description: The page content flows vertically with consistent spacing: section header, then debug settings card, then device information card
assertions.expected: Content appears in order: 'Advanced' header → Debug settings card → Device Information card, with uniform vertical spacing between sections

assertions.description: When content overflows the viewport, the page content area is scrollable
assertions.expected: The settings content area supports vertical scrolling when content exceeds available height

assertions.description: The Debug page is a sub-view within Settings, so it does not have its own tab bar or sidebar navigation — the parent Settings component manages tab selection
assertions.expected: The Debug (Advanced) page content fills the Settings content area directly without any additional tab bar or sidebar
